Split PDF

Extract every page as a separate PDF, or pull out a custom range. Download all as a ZIP. 100% browser — no upload.

✂️
Drop a PDF to split
or click to browse

Split all pages vs custom range — pick the right mode

Split all pages does exactly what it says: every page of your PDF becomes its own separate PDF file. The output is a ZIP containing files named page-1.pdf, page-2.pdf, and so on. Use this when you need to distribute individual pages — separate invoices from a batch export, individual certificates from a combined file, or each page of a signed agreement that different people need to countersign.

Custom range is for when you know exactly which pages you want. Enter page numbers and ranges separated by commas: 1-3, 5, 8-10 produces three output PDFs — one containing pages 1–3, one with just page 5, and one with pages 8–10. Each entry in your list becomes one output file. This is how you extract a chapter from a report, pull one month's statement from a combined annual export, or separate the annexures from the main body of a legal document.

A detail worth knowing: in custom range mode, the numbering is based on the PDF's actual page position, not any printed page numbers inside the document. If your PDF has Roman numerals for the first 10 pages and then restarts at 1, page "1" in the range input always means the first page of the file, not the first "1" printed on a page.

How the splitting works under the hood

The tool uses pdf-lib to read your PDF's internal page structure and copy individual pages into new PDF containers. It doesn't render pages or re-encode any content — it copies the raw page objects. This means text stays selectable, image quality is unchanged, and hyperlinks inside the original PDF are preserved in the split output. The split operation is typically faster than merging or compressing because no pixel-level processing happens.

All output PDFs are packaged into a ZIP using JSZip, also running locally in your browser. Nothing touches a server at any point.

Common situations where splitting a PDF is the right move

Bank statements: Many banks export 12 months as one combined PDF. If you need to submit a specific month for a loan application or rental agreement, use custom range to extract just those pages.

Legal documents: Long agreements where different pages go to different parties — signature pages, schedules, annexures — can be split out individually without printing and re-scanning.

Government portals: Some portals (IRCTC, NSDL, certain state portals) require each supporting document as a separate file. If you've combined everything into one PDF, split it back into its components here.

Scanned books or reports: A scanned textbook or report where you only need specific chapters — extract those page ranges rather than sharing the full document.

What this tool won't do

It won't split password-protected PDFs — encrypted files can't be read by pdf-lib without the password. Remove the password in Adobe Reader first, then split here.

It also won't let you reorder pages within a document or interleave pages from two different PDFs. Splitting only extracts pages in their original order. For page reordering, use PDFsam Basic (free desktop software) or Adobe Acrobat.

Frequently asked questions

Will splitting a PDF reduce its quality?

No. Pages are copied from the source PDF into the output files without any re-encoding. The content is identical — text remains selectable and searchable, images retain their original resolution, and embedded fonts carry over. The only thing that changes is which pages are in which file.

Why do I get a ZIP file instead of individual PDFs?

When a split produces multiple files, a ZIP is the only practical way to download them all at once without your browser firing off dozens of download prompts. Extract the ZIP with Windows Explorer, macOS Finder, or any archive tool (WinRAR, 7-Zip, The Unarchiver) to access your individual PDFs. If you only extracted one page using custom range, you still get a ZIP — it just contains one PDF inside.

Can I extract a single page from a large PDF?

Yes — type just the page number in the custom range box (e.g. 7) and you'll get a one-page PDF. This is the fastest way to pull a specific certificate, invoice, or form page without printing anything.

My PDF has 300 pages. Will this still work?

Yes. Splitting is the lightest PDF operation in terms of browser memory because pages are copied as-is rather than rendered pixel by pixel. A 300-page PDF can typically be split in a few seconds even on a mid-range device. The ZIP packaging of 300 individual files takes a moment longer but works fine.

Does splitting work on mobile?

Yes, though there are two practical limitations on phones: first, the ZIP file needs to be extracted, and not all mobile browsers handle ZIP downloads elegantly — you may need a file manager app. Second, very large PDFs (50MB+) may slow down on phones with limited RAM. For routine document splitting (10–50 pages), mobile works without issues.
